key_traits.label: Life cycle
key_traits.text: Rhizomatous perennial; often persists as a colony or patch with multiple shoots in successive seasons.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Tall upright, usually rough-hairy stems, with leaves numerous along the stem; branching and height vary.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Mostly alternate along the stem; a few lower nodes may be opposite or subopposite. Arrangement alone is not a clean separator from H. annuus.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Long narrow lanceolate blades (commonly ca. 10–30 × 2–5.5 cm), usually folded upward along the midrib (conduplicate) and curving/arching outward or downward; margins usually entire, occasionally finely toothed.

key_traits.label: Leaf venation
key_traits.text: One dominant visible midvein, often producing a trough- or V-shaped blade; contrast broad commonly 3-basal-veined H. annuus.

key_traits.label: Leaf attachment
key_traits.text: Sessile or short-petioled, typically 0–2 cm; inspect a node and compare with the obvious petiole of annual sunflower.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Usually 3–15 yellow-rayed heads, often spaced up the upper stem in a long raceme- or spike-like pattern, rather than just a terminal branching spray.

key_traits.label: Phyllaries
key_traits.text: Long narrow lanceolate bracts (ca. 2–3 mm wide), narrowing gradually into thin, long-attenuate tips; inspect mature head sides and undersides.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Small flattened cypselas with paired scales/awns; not a reliable split from H. annuus.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: long, narrow, often folded V-shaped blade with one strong midvein; very short leaf stalk or sessile insertion; often nearly untoothed margins; upright rhizomatous perennial, often forming colonies; long slender gradually tapering phyllaries beneath heads
